_note: Console texts, in English on purpose. They are printed by the scripts, by the configuration check and by the startup abort — read by whoever installs and operates an instance, often on somebody else's machine, and pasted into search engines when something goes wrong. This file is also the base table every language is laid over (I18n::BASE_LANGUAGE): a key a language file does not carry is answered from here. What the browser shows lives in the language file instead (E-12).

config.file_missing: The configuration file {path} is missing. Run 'install' first, or copy config/config.example.yml to config/config.yml.
config.template_missing: The configuration template {path} is missing. It is part of the delivered package and supplies every default value; without it the application cannot start.
config.unreadable: The configuration file {path} could not be read: {reason}
config.not_a_mapping: The configuration file {path} does not contain a key-value mapping.
config.unknown_key: Unknown key '{key}' in {path}. Only the keys from config/config.example.yml are permitted.
config.aborted: Startup aborted. The configuration is not silently replaced, so that the mistake stays visible.
config.permissions_too_open: Note: {path} is readable by other users (mode {mode}). Expected is 0600: the file names the proxies this instance believes, and widening that list lifts the sign-in limit (SEC-20).

expected.locale: a language code such as 'de' or 'pt-BR', or empty to follow the browser
expected.host: an IP address or a host name
expected.proxy_list: a list of IP addresses or networks, for example ["127.0.0.1", "10.0.0.0/8"]
expected.url: a full address beginning with http:// or https://

startup.schema_too_old: The database is older than the application (at {actual}, expected {expected}). Run 'migrate'.
startup.schema_too_new: The database is newer than the application (at {actual}, expected {expected}). The application does not start, because data would be lost. Install the matching application version.
startup.aborted: Startup aborted. The application does not continue against a schema that does not match it — data would be lost without any error being raised.

environment.title: Checking prerequisites
environment.ruby_missing: Ruby is not present. Install with: {command}
environment.ruby_too_old: Ruby {actual} is too old. At least {expected} is required. Reason: from version 2.9 the sqlite3 gem requires Ruby 3.2 or newer, and versions 3.1 and 3.2 are both out of maintenance. Install with: {command}
environment.node_missing: Node.js is not present. It is needed only to build the frontend, not to run it. Install with: {command}
environment.node_unsuitable: Node.js {actual} does not satisfy the requirement. Needed is {expected}. Note: 'anything from 20 upwards' is not enough — Vite demands exactly this range, so 20.18, 21.x and 22.5 all abort the build. Install with: {command}
environment.npm_missing: npm is not present. It usually comes with Node.js. Install with: {command}
environment.bundler_missing: Bundler is not present. Install with: {command}
environment.lockfile_missing_check: The lockfile {path} is missing. Without it there is no telling which gem versions apply. Run {command}.
environment.gems_missing: The Ruby libraries are not (fully) installed for this machine: {detail} Run {command}. A changed Ruby version leads here as well, because libraries with native parts are built per version.
environment.sqlite_old: Note: the system sqlite3 is at version {actual}. The application does not use it — the sqlite3 gem ships its own library. From {expected} onwards it would be more convenient for running backup and restore by hand. Not an error.
environment.sqlite_missing: Note: the sqlite3 command line tool is not present. The application does not need it. Not an error.
environment.problems_found: {count} prerequisite(s) not satisfied. Carry out the steps named above and check again.

install.title: Installing Prompt Atelier
install.dependencies_failed: Installing the libraries failed — the reason is in the output above. On Windows this is usually a missing DevKit: install Ruby with RubyInstaller **including DevKit** and run this again.
install.configuration_present: config/config.yml already exists and is kept as it is: {path}
install.ask_port: Which port should the application use? [{port}]
install.port_invalid: A port is a whole number from 1 to 65535.
install.port_taken: Port {port} is already in use. Choose a different one.
install.password_mismatch: The two entries do not match.
install.ask_mode: Run portable or as a service? [portable/service, default portable]
install.mode_portable_hint: Portable: start with {command} and stop with Ctrl+C. Nothing is registered with the system.
install.start_failed: The application did not answer. Start it by hand to see the reason: {command}
install.needs_answer: No terminal to ask on, and the answer was not supplied: {question} Use the matching --switch=value.
install.needs_password: No terminal to ask on. Supply the password with --admin-password=...
install.interrupted: Interrupted. Nothing further was changed; running install again continues where it left off.
install.mode_service_failed: The service could not be registered, see above. The installation itself is complete. Start the application with {command} until the service works.
install.dependencies_slow: Installing the Ruby libraries. This takes a few minutes the first time — some of them are compiled from source, which is why Ruby has to be installed with its build tools (on Windows: RubyInstaller with DevKit). Bundler reports each step:
install.answer_empty: That cannot be used. Please try again.
install.answer_unusable: The value supplied with the switch cannot be used.
install.too_many_attempts: Stopping after several attempts. Nothing of what was done before is lost — run install again and it will carry on from here.

service.scope_user: As a user service — no administrator rights needed.
service.scope_system: As a system service — this needs administrator rights.
service.no_systemd: systemctl was not found. This machine has no systemd; use the portable mode (scripts/start_portable.sh).
service.linger_done: Lingering enabled — the service also starts without anybody logging in.
service.linger_failed: The service is set up, but it will only start after somebody logs in. To change that, run as an administrator: {command}
service.no_nssm: The service wrapper is missing: {path}. Ruby scripts cannot be a Windows service on their own. NSSM is a separate program, available from https://nssm.cc. Place nssm.exe in the tools directory named above and run this script again.
service.windows_needs_admin: Creating a Windows service needs an administrator. If this command prompt was not started with "Run as administrator", the service cannot be created and the attempt below will say so.
service.not_created: The service was not created. The wrapper reported no error, but the service does not exist afterwards. The usual reason is missing rights: start a command prompt as an administrator and run scripts\service_install.bat again.
service.already_there: A service named {name} is already registered on this machine. Remove it first with scripts\service_uninstall.bat, then run this script again. It may be left over from an earlier attempt, and a service outlives the directory it was installed from.
service.no_bundle_script: The `bundle` script was not found. Looked in {dir} among others. A service has to be registered against a file that exists, otherwise it registers and never starts. Check that Ruby is installed completely, then run this script again.
service.last_said: What the wrapper said while reporting success: {output}
service.nssm_fallback: As a fallback you can register a scheduled task. It starts at boot but is NOT restarted after a crash, so it is not the same as a service. Run as an administrator:
service.uninstall_failed: The service could not be removed: {path}
service.already_gone: There is no service to remove.
service.data_kept: config/ and data/ were left untouched.

backup.title: Creating a backup
backup.unusable: The backup was written but could not be read back. It has been removed rather than left as a file that looks like a safety net.
backup.failed: The backup could not be created: {reason}
backup.rotated: Removed {count} older backup(s); {keep} are kept. Backups taken before a migration are not touched.

restore.title: Restoring a backup
restore.damaged: This backup cannot be read and was NOT restored: {path}. Restoring a damaged file over a working database is the one mistake with no way back.
restore.still_running: The application is still answering on port {port}. Stop it first — a restore underneath a running instance leaves it writing to a database that no longer exists.
restore.ask_confirm: This overwrites the current database. Type the file name to confirm ({name}):
restore.needs_confirmation: No terminal to confirm on. Repeat with --yes if you are sure you want to overwrite the database with {name}.
restore.safety: The state that was replaced is kept here: {path}

relocate.export_note: The file carries NO passwords. For an exact copy of this instance use backup instead; this format is for moving to another one.
relocate.import_usage: Name the file to import: scripts/import_all.sh <file>
relocate.unreadable: The file is not readable JSON: {reason}
relocate.not_an_instance_export: This is not an instance export. A file exported per workspace belongs in the import inside the application, where collisions can be decided.
relocate.unsupported_version: This file was written by a newer version. Install that version to read it.
relocate.no_users: The file carries no accounts, so there would be nobody to own anything.
relocate.instance_not_empty: This instance already holds accounts. import_all only fills an empty one — merging asks who is who, and that is a question for the per-workspace import inside the application, where somebody can answer it.
relocate.imported: Imported: {count} accounts with their workspaces and prompts.
relocate.passwords_once: One-time passwords, shown ONCE and stored nowhere. Copy them now:
relocate.passwords_change: Everybody has to choose a new password at their first sign-in.

script.already_done: Nothing to do — the desired state is already in place.
script.dependencies_missing: The dependencies are missing. Installing them now.
script.lockfile_missing: Gemfile.lock is missing. Creating it now; from then on the lockfile is binding.
script.config_missing_dev: config/config.yml is missing — creating it from the template.
script.quit_with_ctrl_c: Stop with Ctrl+C. Both processes are stopped together.
script.browser_failed: The browser could not be opened. Address: {address}
script.tests_passed: All tests that ran have passed.
script.backend_failed: The backend did not start. The cause is in the output above. Nothing further is started.
script.gems_unusable: The bundled Ruby libraries cannot be used on this machine, so this script cannot run.
script.gems_unusable_next: Run {command} — it installs the libraries that fit this machine. If that is not possible, use the 'universal' archive of the same version.
script.package_mismatch: This package carries libraries built for {built}, Ruby {series}. This machine is {platform}, Ruby {running}. Libraries with native parts belong to one platform and one Ruby series; take the 'universal' archive of the same version, or let install fetch them.
script.tests_unknown_suite: Unknown suite: {name}. Known: {known}. Nothing was run.
script.tests_unknown_switch: Unknown switch: {name}. Known: {known}. Nothing was run — a switch that is dropped in silence looks like a run that did what you asked.
script.tests_none_ran: No suite ran for the selection {selection}, so nothing was checked. The browser tests need --e2e, the measurements --measure.

migrate.title: Updating the schema
migrate.nothing_to_do: Nothing to do — the schema is up to date. No backup was made.
migrate.rolled_back: Rolled back completely — the data is unchanged.
migrate.database_newer: The database knows steps this version of the application does not: {versions}. That points to a rollback to an older version. Nothing is changed; install the matching application version.

seed.title: Loading example data
seed.confirm: This database will be changed. Continue? [y/N]
seed.skipped: {count} prompts were already there and stayed unchanged.
seed.removed_labels: Along with {keywords} keywords and {tags} tags that nobody uses any more.
seed.nothing_to_remove: There is no example data in "{workspace}".
seed.package_missing: The example package {path} is missing. It is part of the delivered package (BT-17).
seed.package_broken: The example package {path} cannot be read: {reason}
seed.no_database: There is no database at {path} yet. Run 'migrate' first.
seed.schema_outdated: The schema is not up to date (pending: {versions}). Run 'migrate' first.
seed.no_admin: There is no account with instance administrator rights. Run the initial setup.
seed.ambiguous: Several instance administrators exist: {emails}. Name the address you mean with --email.

reset_password.title: Emergency access: reset password
reset_password.mismatch: The two entries do not match.
reset_password.no_admin: There is no account with instance administrator rights. Run the initial setup.
reset_password.ambiguous: Several instance administrators exist: {emails}. Name the address you mean as an argument.
reset_password.must_change: A new password must be chosen at the next sign-in.
reset_password.sessions_dropped: Every existing session of this account has been discarded.

build.title: Building the delivery package
build.lockfile_missing: {path} is missing. Without it npm would resolve the dependencies afresh, and the package would not be the one that was tested.
build.tests_skipped: Tests skipped on request. The package is not release-grade; the VERSION file says so.
build.tests_failed: The tests failed. No package was written — an archive built over a failing test is one nobody can tell apart from a good one.
build.npm_ci: Installing the frontend dependencies from the lockfile (npm ci) ...
build.frontend_empty: The frontend build produced no index.html in {path}.
build.source_missing: Missing from the source tree: {path}. It belongs in the package as {target}.
build.optional_missing: Not present and therefore not included: {path}
build.optional_missing_tools: Without tools/nssm.exe the Windows service setup falls back to a scheduled task on every machine — it starts at boot but is NOT restarted after a crash.
build.gems_missing: No vendored gems in {path}. Run bundle install, or build the universal shape only with --shape=universal.
build.gems_copied: Gems included for {platform}, Ruby {ruby}. This package installs without a network — on that platform and that Ruby series only.
build.done: Build complete. The archives are in {path}.

portable.title: Starting Prompt Atelier
portable.stop_hint: Stop with Ctrl+C. A backup is taken on the way out; --no-backup leaves it out.
portable.ended_badly: The application ended with exit code {code}. The reason is in the output above.
portable.no_database_yet: No database yet, so there is nothing to back up. Run install first.
portable.port_taken: Port {port} is already in use — most likely by an instance that is still running. Close its window, or wait a moment and try again. Nothing was started.

password.too_short: The password must be at least {minimum} characters long.
password.too_long: The password must be at most {maximum} characters long.
password.too_common: This password is on the list of commonly used passwords and is therefore not allowed.
password.wrong_current: The current password is not correct.
password.changed: The password was changed. All other sessions were ended.

package.title: Packing this installation for another machine
package.collected: Collected: application, libraries, built interface, scripts, examples.
package.skipping: Not present in this installation and therefore not packed: {name}
package.no_gems: The Ruby libraries are not in this installation (app/vendor/bundle).
package.no_interface: The built interface is not in this installation (app/public/index.html).
package.run_install_first: Run install first — a package made from a half-installed instance installs a half-installed instance.
package.private_file: Refused: {path} would have been packed. Nothing was written. This is a mistake in the script, please report it.
package.done_hint: It carries neither your configuration nor your data — it installs a fresh instance on a machine of the same platform and Ruby series, without a network.

measure.title: Measuring Prompt Atelier
measure.bench: Bench: {path} — own directory, own database, own port. The instance you operate is not touched.
measure.step_stock: Step 1 of 5: building a stock of {count} prompts
measure.step_stock_kept: Step 1 of 5: keeping the stock of {count} prompts already on the bench (--reseed builds it again)
measure.step_server: Step 2 of 5: starting the bench instance
measure.server_silent: The bench instance did not answer within {seconds} seconds. Nothing was measured.
measure.step_measurements: Step 3 of 5: measurements, {runs} runs per case
measure.missed: {requirement} missed: {case}. Raise the thread pool in config/puma.rb before the requirement is changed.
measure.needs_positive: --prompts and --runs both need a number greater than zero.
measure.too_few: {case} found {found} prompts, and the case needs {expected}. Nothing was measured — a fast answer over an empty result is not a result.
measure.not_answered: {path} answered {code}. A measurement over a failing request would be a number about nothing.
measure.step_load: Step 4 of 5: under load — {users} clients ({writers} saving), {think} s mean think time, {seconds} s
measure.load_result: {case}: server p95 {p95} ms (limit {limit} ms), client saw {client} ms, {requests} requests, {rate}/s, {errors} errors
measure.load_no_targets: The stock holds too few prompts for the writing clients. Measure with more prompts, or with --no-load.
measure.load_silent: {case} sent no request at all in the whole window. Nothing was measured.
measure.errors: {case}: {count} requests did not answer 200 ({kinds}). TF-706 asks for no write errors, and that cannot be read off a duration.
measure.load_ceiling: And once more with no think time at all, {seconds} s — the throughput ceiling, not a verdict.
measure.load_result_ceiling: {case}: {rate} requests/s, server p95 {p95} ms (not gated), client saw {client} ms, {errors} errors
measure.no_server_timings: {case}: the bench instance handed out no timings of its own. Nothing was measured — the client stopwatch is not a substitute, it measures its own scheduling as much as the server.
measure.serving_account: Sign in as {email} with the password {password}
measure.serving_stock: The workspace "Marketing" holds a share of the {count} prompts; pick it in the workspace menu.
measure.serving_stop: Stop with Ctrl+C. The bench is kept (--serve implies --keep); remove it by hand or with --reseed on the next run.
